{"consolidated_memory":"## Recurring Partial Upload Issue in storage/blob/uploader.rs

**Component**: storage/blob/uploader.rs (storage side, Rust stack)
**Common Symptom**: A final part in upload never gets acknowledged
**Common Repro**: Upload 40 MB fixture over throttled link
**Test Coverage**: Module test block in storage/blob/uploader.rs

This recurring issue manifested in 5 separate occasions, each with distinct triggers and root causes:

### Occasion 1: [2026-02-04] Corporate proxy traffic (PR #2640, fix/partial-upload-1)
- **Trigger**: Traffic arriving through corporate proxy
- **Root Cause**: Unbounded retry loop with no backoff
- **Fix**: Capped retry attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter
- **Outcome**: 56 duplicate rows per day stopped being written

### Occasion 2: [2026-03-13] Large payload threshold (PR #4098, fix/partial-upload-2)
- **Trigger**: Payloads above roughly 2 MB
- **Root Cause**: Config loader reading wrong environment file
- **Fix**: Made environment selection explicit and failed closed on ambiguity
- **Outcome**: Backlog cleared 12 minutes after deploy

### Occasion 3: [2026-04-11] Empty input list (PR #5324, fix/partial-upload-3)
- **Trigger**: Input list came in empty
- **Root Cause**: Naive datetime compared against timezone-aware datetime
- **Fix**: Made every boundary timezone aware at the edge
- **Outcome**: Throughput rose 8 percent, to 847 requests per second

### Occasion 4: [2026-07-14] Concurrent requests on same key (PR #5959, fix/partial-upload-4)
- **Trigger**: Two requests raced on the same key
- **Root Cause**: Missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- **Fix**: Normalised to NFC ahead of the digest
- **Outcome**: P99 latency fell from 5.6 seconds to 87 milliseconds

### Occasion 5: [2026-08-15] Non-ASCII record names (PR #8022, fix/partial-upload-6)
- **Trigger**: Records carrying non-ASCII names
- **Root Cause**: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- **Fix**: Raised pool ceiling and added bounded wait queue in front of it
- **Outcome**: Flaky test went from 97 failures per 100 runs to zero"}
